The petitioners vide the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 seek quashing of FIR No.0352/2022 dated 27.07.2022 registered under Sections 498A/506/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 at PS.: Chhawala, District Dwarka, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom in view of the Settlement Deed dated 04.02.2023 arrived at between the parties.

2. This petition is accompanied by of the Settlement Deed dated 04.02.2023 and is also supported by affidavits of all the petitioners and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
3. Petitioner nos.1 to 4 and as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the Investigating Officer.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.
4. Issue Notice.
5. Learned APP accepts notice.
He confirms that he has no objection to the quashing of the FIR.
CRL.M.C. 6868/2023 page 1 of 2

Learned counsel for the respondent no.2 also accepts notice.
Respondent no.2 confirms that the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have been granted divorce by mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 07.06.2023.

She further affirms of the Settlement Deed dated 04.02.2023 whereby the petitioner no.1 has already paid her a sum of Rs.6,10,000/- and the remaining amount of Pradeep Tyagi & Ors vs State & Anr on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14415010/

7. In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors.
Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr.(2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr.(2014) 6 SCC 466

8. Accordingly, the petition is allowed and FIR No.0352/2022 dated 27.07.2022 registered under Sections 498A/506/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 at PS.: Chhawala, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom are quashed.
9. Accordingly, the present petition, alongwith the pending applications, if any, stands disposed of.
